tasks.short: Plan project activities, dependencies and dates, then agree and publish the schedule.

steps.what: Read the project brief and identify deliverables, constraints and required dates.

loop.input: Approved project brief and a fixed requirements schema.
loop.output: Draft planning requirements with source passages and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate the schema and source references; the project manager checks commitments and omissions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per brief; unreadable or ambiguous sections go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Deliverables and constraints often appear in narrative text. Structured briefs need only configuration.

steps.what: Check existing tasks, resource availability and delivery commitments.
Agree dependencies, effort assumptions and competing priorities with workstream leads.
Build the draft schedule and compare feasible sequencing options.
Agree the schedule baseline and approve delivery commitments.
Publish the approved schedule and notify task owners.

tasks.design: A bounded reader turns the approved brief in {DOCS} into draft planning requirements with source references. An integration supplies availability and commitments to the scheduling functions in {PROJECT}, which calculate options from agreed assumptions. The sponsor approves commitments before {WORKFLOW} publishes the baseline and sends internal notifications.
tasks.previous_blocker: The scheduling functions already existed, but briefs, availability and cross-team commitments were disconnected. Building and maintaining the connections competed with delivery work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building adapters and validation. Bounded extraction can handle narrative briefs, while existing scheduling functions handle dates and dependencies.
tasks.still_hard: Effort estimates, hidden dependencies and contested priorities remain uncertain. Resource levelling may need custom deterministic code if the existing {PROJECT} lacks suitable functions.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager gets credible commitments from people and explains which trade-offs the sponsor must make.

ambition.what: Twice-weekly sequencing decisions for blocked critical-path work.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less brief transcription and schedule maintenance, with more time for dependency negotiations. The project manager gains authority to propose sequencing alternatives; sponsor approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Check production capacity before promising project delivery dates.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, lead times and how operational commitments constrain project schedules.

reach.task: Compare the cost and delivery impact of schedule alternatives.
reach.learn: Scenario assumptions, sensitivity analysis and defensible comparisons.

evidence.claim: Dependency scheduling, baselines and notifications are established capabilities; availability integration depends on installed systems.
The proposed bounded extraction and time reductions are design estimates, not demonstrated outcomes for this job.
The digest documents an AI-assisted report with nonexistent citations, supporting source checks for generated planning requirements.

assumptions: This describes a hybrid mid-size European company using {PROJECT} and briefs in {DOCS}.
The existing {PROJECT} supports dependencies, calendars and baseline publication.
Time shares and remaining percentages are estimates guided by the supplied priors.
Availability uses working capacity and leave dates, without medical details.
Build ranges cover a pilot and reusable templates; shared components across tasks are built once.
Access and consultation ranges represent working effort; external waiting can extend elapsed time.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules determine employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Which scheduling and resource functions are enabled in the installed {PROJECT}.
Whether availability and task records have reliable identifiers and accessible interfaces.
Who may approve baselines and change delivery commitments.
Which national consultation requirements apply to staffing-data use.
research_questions: Can native scheduling functions represent the required capacity and dependency constraints?
How accurately does bounded extraction preserve commitments in representative briefs?
Do schedule options remain useful when effort estimates are expressed as ranges?
new_work: Review extracted commitments and unresolved questions.
Maintain calendar mappings and scheduling constraints.
Handle stale availability records and failed integrations.
Check that published baselines match approved versions.

tasks.short: Request project updates, assess blockers and agree action before deadlines slip.

steps.what: Check which tasks need updates against the published schedule.
Request missing updates and chase late responses.
Read responses and identify changed dates, blockers and unanswered questions.

loop.input: Replies to update requests, task identifiers and the published schedule.
loop.output: Draft progress summary and blocker list with source references.
loop.check: Validate task identifiers and dates; distinguish reported facts from missing information and conflicting statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per update batch; contradictions and unmatched tasks go to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Legacy replies contain narrative blockers and qualified dates. Structured status fields use deterministic processing.

steps.what: Discuss uncertain progress and blockers with task owners.
Choose recovery actions within delegated limits and flag required escalations.
Record confirmed progress, recovery actions and escalation requests.

tasks.design: Configure {PROJECT} and {WORKFLOW} to request structured updates when records become stale, with controlled reminders through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. A bounded reader summarises narrative replies and links each statement to its source. The project manager confirms uncertain progress and approves recovery actions before confirmed records update {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrived in different formats, and reminders were detached from task records. Missing information still required conversations, making partial automation seem less worthwhile.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and reminders can handle routine collection. Small adapters and bounded extraction can connect legacy replies to task records without automating recovery decisions.
tasks.still_hard: A response can be timely yet misleading. People may lack reliable estimates, conceal difficulties or need help resolving dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager creates enough trust for people to report trouble early and negotiates practical recovery commitments.

ambition.what: Daily escalation decisions for newly blocked critical tasks.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from chasing and copying updates to short blocker discussions and recovery choices. Decision rights expand only if the sponsor delegates specific escalation thresholds or recovery limits.

reach.task: Coordinate follow-ups and maintain the action register.
reach.learn: Task ownership, escalation routes and how to distinguish missing updates from unresolved decisions.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of project delays.
reach.learn: Consistent blocker categories and analysis that separates reporting delays from delivery delays.

evidence.claim: Structured update forms, stale-record checks and internal reminders can usually be configured without a model.
Narrative updates can support bounded extraction, but reported completion and recovery choices still need human confirmation.
The proposed design and time reductions are estimates; the digest contains no direct project-update implementation case.

assumptions: Task owners provide updates in {PROJECT} and in replies through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}.
Mailbox work is estimated from this mixed reporting process; the supplied mail share is a weak prior.
Reminders are internal, rate-limited and stop when a valid update arrives.
Recovery actions stay within existing delegation; escalation requests do not themselves change commitments.
Time shares include project-manager participation in discussions and approvals.
Build ranges cover one reporting process and exclude external waiting.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules may require consultation if reporting becomes employee monitoring.
unknowns: How often owners update structured fields rather than send narrative replies.
Whether update threads reliably identify projects and tasks.
Which recovery actions the project manager may approve.
Whether current reporting is used for individual employee evaluation.
research_questions: Does a structured update form reduce missing information without increasing owner effort?
Can extraction preserve tentative dates and distinguish commitments from aspirations?
What reminder cadence improves response rates without creating notification fatigue?
new_work: Review extracted dates, contradictions and unmatched updates.
Maintain stale-update thresholds and reminder schedules.
Resolve failed deliveries and missing owners.
Check that reporting stays within its agreed purpose and access scope.

tasks.short: Track milestones and delivery evidence, assess readiness and record acceptance or exceptions.

steps.what: Check milestone dates, owners and acceptance criteria in the project records.
Locate submitted deliverables, test results and approval records.
Read evidence against acceptance criteria and identify gaps.

loop.input: Textual delivery evidence and approved acceptance criteria.
loop.output: Draft criterion-to-evidence map, apparent gaps and uncertain matches.
loop.check: Verify source passages and document versions; a person checks each claimed match and unresolved criterion.
loop.stop: One mapping and one repair attempt per deliverable; unsupported formats and ambiguous criteria go to specialist review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative evidence may describe criteria in different words. Exact test results and signed approvals use deterministic checks.

steps.what: Refresh the milestone variance sheet using dates, progress and evidence gaps.
Review readiness with the deliverable owner and obtain the acceptance decision.
Record the approved milestone status and notify owners of exceptions.

tasks.design: An integration links milestone records in {PROJECT} to versioned evidence in {DOCS}, while deterministic calculations replace the variance workbook with a {BI} view. A bounded loop maps narrative evidence to acceptance criteria and shows unresolved gaps. Approved acceptance decisions update {PROJECT} and trigger exception notifications through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were structured, but evidence links and acceptance records were scattered. A separate workbook reconciled them, and automated status could not establish genuine readiness.
tasks.enabler_now: Document identifiers and accessible interfaces make evidence indexing practical. AI-assisted coding can simplify the integration work, with bounded reading reserved for narrative evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Evidence quality, vague acceptance criteria and specialist testing remain costly. A complete document set does not establish that the deliverable works.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager challenges optimistic status claims and brings the right specialist into acceptance decisions.

ambition.what: A self-service milestone readiness view for small internal project owners.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence searching and workbook reconciliation, with more attention to disputed readiness and upcoming handovers. Acceptance rights remain with the accountable deliverable owner.

reach.task: Define evidence needed to accept a deliverable.
reach.learn: Test coverage, traceability and the difference between evidence presence and demonstrated quality.

reach.task: Maintain versioned delivery and approval records.
reach.learn: Document identifiers, retention rules and reliable evidence links.

evidence.claim: Milestone variance calculations and evidence indexing are deterministic when identifiers and baseline dates are reliable.
Narrative evidence mapping can assist review but cannot replace specialist tests or accountable acceptance.
The proposed implementation and remaining-time estimates have no direct documented case in the supplied digest.

assumptions: This typical hybrid process uses a {SPREADSHEET} to reconcile milestone dates and document evidence.
The workbook is integration glue; the authoritative schedule remains in {PROJECT}.
Deliverables have stable identifiers and approved acceptance criteria.
The bounded loop handles textual evidence; specialist technical validation stays separate.
The dashboard labels unreviewed assessments as provisional.
Build ranges cover a pilot with a limited set of evidence formats and exclude external waiting.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access to personal data and any national consultation requirements need local assessment.
unknowns: Whether milestone tracking actually uses a workbook or native {PROJECT} reporting.
How consistently documents identify their project, milestone and version.
Which roles approve acceptance and whether approvals are recorded.
Which evidence formats require specialist systems or restricted access.
research_questions: Can deterministic metadata checks reliably identify missing or obsolete evidence?
Does narrative mapping falsely treat partial evidence as satisfying a criterion?
Can the readiness view help occasional project owners identify the next required action?
new_work: Maintain evidence mappings and acceptance templates.
Repair broken links and obsolete document references.
Audit provisional statuses and recorded acceptance decisions.

tasks.short: Agree who owns project work, confirm capacity and record responsibilities.

steps.what: Review unassigned tasks, required skills and existing responsibilities.
Reconcile staff availability and existing allocations in the capacity sheet.
Discuss suitable ownership, workload and support needs with staff.
Resolve competing demands and approve staff allocation with the line manager.
Explain responsibilities, decision limits and handovers to the assigned staff.
Record agreed ownership and responsibilities in the project records.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration combines declared availability from {HCM} with assignments in {PROJECT} to replace the capacity workbook. People discuss ownership and approve allocation, then configured forms in {PROJECT} capture responsibilities and publish agreed records. No model is needed for this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity data crossed organisational boundaries and often needed manual correction. Selecting an owner depended on context that a capacity sheet could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations and existing assignment forms can remove reconciliation and recording effort. These improvements do not depend on automated staff selection.
tasks.still_hard: Fair workload, development opportunities, specialist fit and competing line-management priorities remain human judgements. GDPR and national employment and consultation rules shape access to staffing data.
tasks.human_edge: The project manager recognises when someone needs support, negotiates competing demands and establishes clear responsibility without damaging trust.
tasks.altitude: The week gains some time from capacity checks and recording, while allocation discussions remain substantial. Nothing changes in decision rights; line managers still approve staff commitments.

reach.task: Resolve shared-service capacity conflicts across projects.
reach.learn: Service priorities, allocation limits and how project commitments affect routine operations.

reach.task: Agree technical ownership and handover responsibilities.
reach.learn: Technical skill requirements, review duties and the boundaries between delivery and operational ownership.

evidence.claim: Declared capacity and current allocations can be reconciled deterministically; choosing staff still requires contextual judgement.
Keeping employee selection human and omitting model-based ranking avoids introducing AI selection into this design.
The proposed effort reductions are estimates; the supplied digest contains no direct staff-allocation implementation case.

assumptions: A capacity workbook connects {HCM} availability to assignments in {PROJECT}.
Only declared availability and agreed allocations are needed; medical details are excluded.
Line managers approve staff commitments in this typical matrix organisation.
The low-drudgery prior is retained: most time stays in discussion, allocation and explanation.
The integration identifies capacity conflicts but does not score employee performance or select workers.
Build ranges cover one staffing pool and exclude external waiting.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules determine consultation and employment requirements.
unknowns: Whether the organisation uses matrix allocation or delegates assignment rights to project managers.
How reliable availability and allocation records are across projects.
Which staffing fields project managers may access.
Whether the proposed integration requires employee or works-council consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which capacity checks catch double-booking without exposing unnecessary employee data?
Can native assignment forms capture decision limits and handovers clearly?
Does the capacity view support fair allocation without encouraging excessive utilisation?
new_work: Review conflicting or stale capacity records.
Maintain allocation calendars and access permissions.
Record approved exceptions to capacity limits.
Check that responsibility records match the agreements made with staff.

role.altitude: The project manager spends less time reconciling records and more time negotiating dependencies, resolving blockers and challenging readiness. Wider authority requires explicit sponsor or line-manager delegation; automation alone grants none.
reach: Production planning: connect project promises to real operational capacity.
Quality management: define acceptance evidence and organise specialist review.
Management analysis: compare recovery options and identify recurring delay causes.
Administrative services: coordinate shared capacity and reliable action records.
skills_to_grow: Clear acceptance criteria and evidence review.
Data quality, integration ownership and exception handling.
Privacy-aware use of staffing data and national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Run a small delivery-assurance service that gives occasional project owners schedule options, early blocker reviews and evidence-backed readiness views, with named people retaining commitment and acceptance decisions.
